theater.title: North Korea
theater.sub: The options the US has toward North Korea, and what followed the last times the US (often with South Korea and Japan) did something like each one.
theater.proxy_note: Every reply here is an act by North Korea itself. KCNA and Rodong Sinmun are used only as labelled claims of what North Korea says; launches are dated by South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff or Japan's Defense Ministry as reported by an allowed outlet.
theater.hold_note: Hold cases are weeks from Jan 20, 2025 on (the start of the second Trump term) with no logged US sanctions, drill, deployment, missile-defense or posture move. Weeks inside the Sep 12 - Oct 12, 2026 dense-launch stretch and two weeks of Ulchi Freedom Shield 2025 and one week of Freedom Edge 2025 (US moves that an allowed outlet reports but the log does not hold) are left out. The log is a sample, not a full list: it says that many launches and some US moves are missing, so a week that looks quiet may only be a week where nothing was logged. Read option A as a rough sketch and do not compare it number-for-number with options that rest on a few well-reported cases.
theater.not_measured: Economic effects (sanctions relief, trade, prices) are not measured for North Korea; that category is left out of the index. Strain with South Korea, Japan and China is not measured either.
presets: Launch after carrier and DMZ visits
theater.under_logged: The log is a sample. It starts in March 1993, but 1995-97, 2004, 2007-08, 2011 and 2014-15 are thinly logged, and the 1993-2015 years hold only a few Treasury rounds and short-range launches. 2020 and most of 2021 are empty, and many launches from 2022 on are missing, so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.
theater.claim_note: North Korean state media (KCNA, Rodong Sinmun)

intensity.name: Tension level
intensity.note: Tension level counts logged North Korean launches, tests and provocations (not threatening statements) in the 14 days before each date: 2 points each, +2 if someone died. The log is a sample, so quiet stretches are understated.

rule.other: Counts when anyone was reported hurt in a North Korean reply (a launch, test or provocation) within 7 days of the US move.

escalation.name: Escalation
escalation.trigger: Share of past cases followed by a North Korean missile launch, nuclear test or provocation within 7 days. Some of these replies are threatening statements the log files as provocations (for example #2049), not launches.
escalation.other: Share of past cases followed by a North Korean missile launch, nuclear test or provocation within 7 days (timing only). A threatening statement the log files as a provocation counts.
escalation.hold: Share of hold weeks followed by a North Korean missile launch, nuclear test or provocation within 7 days (timing only). A threatening statement the log files as a provocation counts.

rule.trigger: Counts when North Korea launched a missile, tested a nuclear weapon or provoked within 7 days (a clear link or timing only). A threatening statement the log files as a provocation counts.
rule.other: Counts when North Korea launched, tested or provoked anywhere within 7 days (timing only, not shown to be a reply). A threatening statement the log files as a provocation counts.

military.name: Military cost
military.reply: Share of past cases where North Korea's reply was a ballistic missile or ICBM.
military.strike: Share of hold weeks with a North Korean ballistic missile or ICBM launch in the 7 days after.
military.none: No direct military cost is counted for the move itself, so this counts as 0%.

rule.reply: Counts when the reply was a ballistic missile or ICBM. A satellite rocket, a cruise missile, "projectiles", a nuclear test, drones and statements do not count.
rule.strike: Counts when a North Korean ballistic missile or ICBM was launched in the 7 days after the Monday.

economic.name: Economic harm
economic.other: Not measured for North Korea. There is no clear measure of sanctions relief, trade or prices in the log, so this category is shown as "not measured" and left out of the index.
economic.rule: Not measured. Nothing is counted for this category.

political.name: Political / diplomatic
political.other: Share of past cases NOT followed within 14 days by talks (a summit, a meeting or an offer to meet) between the US and North Korea. Statements and threats do not count.
political.rule: Counts when no talks (a summit, a meeting or an offer to meet) between the US and North Korea were logged within 14 days after the move. Statements, threats and appeals do not count as talks. Rule changed on 2026-10-26.

hostile.title: An unarmed OH-58 strays into North Korea near the DMZ and is shot down. North Korea says it shot down an 'enemy helicopter'. Chief Warrant Officer David Hilemon is killed and Bobby Hall is held; Hall is released on Dec 29. Dated Dec 17: the Dec 18 report says only 'Saturday'
North Korea fires a multistage Taepodong-1 missile over Japan and into the Pacific Ocean (NPR chronology)
That week North Korea removes IAEA seals and cameras at its nuclear facilities and orders the inspectors out of the country (CBS, CNN)
Four North Korean MiG fighters intercept a US Air Force RC-135S reconnaissance aircraft. CBS (Mar 4) says 'Sunday', which is Mar 2; NPR dates the intercept Mar 1
North Korea fires a short-range anti-ship cruise missile on Monday, Mar 10 (PBS, Mar 11); an earlier one was fired on Feb 24. Day set from the weekday in the PBS report
North Korea launches seven missiles, including a long-range Taepodong-2 that fails (CNN). NPR's chronology lists the launch for July 5
North Korea announces and carries out its first nuclear test. President Bush calls it a provocative act and says the world will respond
North Korea launches a long-range rocket. The White House statement and CNN report the launch; North Korea says it was a satellite launch
North Korea carries out a second nuclear test; world leaders condemn it (PBS NewsHour)
The South Korean warship Cheonan is sunk near Baengnyeong Island. A South Korean-led investigation, announced May 20, says a North Korean torpedo did it. Logged on the date of the sinking
North Korea shells Yeonpyeong island; the island's residents recount the attack and two more bodies are found (AP)
North Korea's long-range rocket launch fails. The White House says the US will not give food aid after the launch (CBS, AP)
North Korea launches a long-range rocket; the UN and many governments condemn it (NPR, CNN)
North Korea carries out a third nuclear test; the White House calls it highly provocative (NBC)
North Korea bars South Korean workers from the Kaesong industrial zone (NPR)
The FBI says North Korea is behind the Sony Pictures cyber attack; President Obama vows a response (Al Jazeera, NPR)
North and South Korea trade fire across the border (NPR). On Aug 4, two South Korean soldiers were wounded by mines
North Korea claims a successful hydrogen bomb test (ABC)
North Korea launches a long-range rocket from Dongchang-ri (AP, CBS). North Korea says it was a satellite launch
Two Scud missiles are fired and fly about 300 miles (CBS timeline, citing the BBC). US date in the timeline
Two mid-range Nodong ballistic missiles are fired and fly about 500 miles (CBS timeline, citing South Korea's Joint Chiefs)
A submarine-launched ballistic missile is fired off the east coast; Seoul says it appeared to explode at about 10 km (CBS timeline). US date in the timeline
North Korea carries out its fifth and biggest nuclear test; it draws global outrage (PBS NewsHour)
North Korea fires an intermediate-range Polaris-2 (KN-15) ballistic missile into the East Sea, its first launch of 2017
North Korea fires four extended-range Scud ballistic missiles toward Japan. US THAAD parts reach Osan the same evening (The War Zone); that move is not logged on its own
A Hwasong-12 ballistic missile launch fails very early (CBS timeline)
North Korea launches a Hwasong-12 ballistic missile that flies about 400 miles; it CLAIMS it could carry a nuclear warhead (NPR, CBS timeline)
North Korea fires a medium-range ballistic missile in what AFP calls a fresh test (AFP, CBS timeline)
North Korea CLAIMS its first successful ICBM test, the Hwasong-14 (Al Jazeera, CBS timeline)
North Korea fires a second ICBM that flies longer and higher than the first; it says the whole US is in range (AP, CBS timeline)
North Korea launches three unidentified short-range missiles within 30 minutes; one likely exploded soon after take-off (CBS timeline)

A Hwasong-12 ballistic missile flies over Hokkaido, Japan; South Korea says it flew 1,677 miles to a height of 341 miles. Dated Aug 29 by Japan and Seoul; the CBS timeline lists it as Aug 28 (US date)

Sixth nuclear test at 12:29 p.m. local time; Seoul puts the quake at magnitude 5.7 and USGS at 6.3. North Korea CLAIMS a hydrogen bomb of 'tens to hundreds of kilotons'. Dated by AP from Seoul and USGS, not by the JCS
A new ICBM launched about 3:17 a.m. local time; the Pentagon's first read is an ICBM that splashed down in Japan's EEZ; the JCS confirmed the launch. First launch in about 2.5 months
The JCS reports several projectiles flying up to about 125 miles; not yet confirmed as banned ballistic missiles. Amid stalled US-DPRK talks after the failed Hanoi summit
Two suspected short-range missiles from Sino-ri and Kusong flew 260 and 167 miles, per the JCS

The JCS says North Korea fired unidentified projectiles twice from near its west coast across the country into eastern waters, a day after the drills began. AP's text says 'Tuesday' (Aug 6) while the page is dated Aug 5 (US time); logged Aug 6 Korea time. Followed a Jul 25 short-range ballistic launch and two rocket-artillery tests

hostile.actor: North Korea (per JCS and US officials)
hostile.title: Two cruise missiles fired Sunday (Mar 21), per the JCS ('cruise missiles, not ballistic'); US officials call them short-range and not covered by UN bans. Biden: 'nothing much has changed'

Two SRBMs fired about 11 minutes apart from North Pyongan, flying about 430 km, the third launch that month. Hours before, North Korea CLAIMS (via its state media, as AP reports) the US sanctions show a 'confrontational stance' and warned of stronger action

North Korea fires an ICBM, its first since 2017, detected by the South Korean and Japanese militaries; state media reported it the next day. The US then announced new sanctions on five entities and people in Russia and North Korea (State spokesperson; exact date not given by AP)

Three missiles from Sunan hours after Biden ended his Asia trip: a suspected ICBM (about 360 km, 540 km apogee), one that failed after 20 km, and an SRBM (760 km). The US and South Korea fired two missiles in reply

An SRBM from Taechon flies about 600 km, apogee 60 km, per the JCS; it came as the Reagan arrived. Stripes: the 18th round of missile tests that year, a record. Start of the Sep 25 - Nov 2, 2022 dense-launch window

Two SRBMs from the Sunan area of Pyongyang flew about 360 km; JCS reported them between 18:10 and 18:20 local time; Japan's coast guard confirmed citing the defense ministry. Day before Vice President Harris arrived in Seoul

Japan's Defense Ministry says a ballistic missile was launched at 7:22 a.m. and passed over Japan at 7:29 a.m.; residents told to take cover. The ABC page shows Oct 4 and its metadata Oct 3 (UTC); logged Oct 4 Japan time
At least 23 missiles, one landing about 100 miles from a South Korean island and triggering air-raid sirens there; the most in a single day
Five North Korean drones cross into the South; one reaches the northern Seoul area; South Korea scrambles jets and fires warning shots. First drone incursion since 2017

Two ballistic missiles early Wednesday (Jul 19 Korea time, hours after the Kentucky arrived): Japan says ranges of 550 and 600 km, 50 km apogee, outside Japan's EEZ. The launch followed a Hwasong-18 ICBM test nearly a week earlier

A rocket launched at 3:50 a.m. from Tongchang-ri; Japan issues a J-Alert as it flies over Okinawa; the JCS detects it; North Korea says the satellite attempt failed. Date taken from NPR's 'Thursday' and the exercise start

hostile.actor: North Korea (per JCS and Japan MoD)
hostile.title: A satellite rocket is launched at 10:42 p.m.; the JCS says US, South Korean and Japanese Aegis ships tracked it; Japan's MoD says the rocket separated and fell outside its EEZ. USNI wrote it up Nov 22
An ICBM launch on a Monday; AP gives only the weekday, so Dec 18 is inferred from the Wednesday, Dec 20 drill. Preceded the trilateral bomber drill
The JCS says the missile flew about 1,000 km; North Korea CLAIMS a successful solid-fuel hypersonic test

hostile.actor: North Korea (per South Korea's defense ministry and JCS)
hostile.title: A satellite rocket explodes about two minutes after liftoff (10:46 p.m.); the JCS says US, South Korean and Japanese Aegis destroyers were collecting launch data. Fourth satellite attempt in 12 months
The JCS says a missile launched at 5:30 a.m. from near Pyongyang exploded after about 155 miles and calls it a failed launch; North Korea CLAIMS a successful test of multiple warheads

Two missiles launched 10 minutes apart; the first flew about 600 km, the second about 120 km and may have exploded. A day earlier North Korea CLAIMED it would respond with 'offensive and overwhelming' action to the drills. First launch in five days
North Korea's longest-flying ICBM test so far (higher and longer than any earlier launch); South Korea's military says it may be solid-fuel. A military spokesperson (not the JCS by name) spoke
The JCS says the missile flew about 1,100 km while Secretary of State Blinken was in Seoul; North Korea CLAIMS 1,500 km, 12 times the speed of sound

hostile.actor: North Korea (per JCS and Japan MoD)
hostile.title: One SRBM at 12:35 p.m.; South Korea says 700 km, Japan's MoD about 50 km altitude and 450+ km. The sixth ballistic launch of 2025. The same day North Korea's defense minister CLAIMED the Hegseth DMZ visit fans 'war hysteria'

Start of the Sep 12 - Oct 12, 2026 dense-launch window. Date and type come from a Sep 22 page, not the JCS release

hostile.title: Two SRBMs about three hours apart flew about 279 and 373 miles; Japan's Defense Ministry reported a suspected launch outside its territorial waters. North Korea CLAIMS a 'new-type weapon' and a 560+ mile path, which Seoul disputes

hostile.title: Two explosions wound three South Korean soldiers; the UN Command and Seoul find a North Korean anti-personnel mine and an armistice violation. Kim Yo Jong calls the finding a 'conspiratorial farce'. North Korea denies planting the mines
Reuters says the last North Korean ballistic launch before Oct 12 was Oct 3; state media (KCNA) CLAIMED a hypersonic missile Kim oversaw. Date comes from the Oct 12 Reuters story, not a JCS release

Multiple missiles of different types launched about 9:20 a.m.; one flew more than 900 km; Japan's coast guard reported two projectiles that fell. The JCS called it a show of force responding to South Korea's first hypersonic test. Fourth launch in a month, 10+ tests in 2026
